faq.q: How do you keep feed dry in a steel shed?
faq.a: Through a tight roof, good sheet laps and steady ventilation.

blocks.text: A dairy farm stores feed in bulk, and the feed must stay dry. This shed gives Dravton Dairy a covered store beside its animal housing. Steel Mind designed it as a pre-engineered building and erected it on site.
A tight roof and good sheet laps keep rain out. Ridge vents or louvers keep air moving above the feed. Wide openings allow trucks and loaders to enter. The 17-foot height leaves room for tall stacks.
Many dairy clients return to add feed storage after the first shed. Dravton Dairy is one example, and bolted PEB frames make this kind of addition simple.
